key_insight: Physis-Lang argues that language can serve as a physical representation for video world models if it is allowed to evolve with the task, rather than being treated as a fixed description tool. The core breakthrough is a self-evolving language framework that aims to encode physical knowledge more explicitly and improve physically consistent video prediction.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the gap between visually plausible video generation and physically correct world modeling. It targets the common failure where models produce realistic-looking scenes that still violate basic physical principles such as motion, interaction, and causality.
method: Introduce Physis-Lang, a self-evolving language representation designed to capture physical dynamics.
Use language as the primary physical state representation instead of relying only on extra visual, latent, numerical, or planning signals.
Adapt and refine the language over time so it can better express the physical regularities needed for video world prediction.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this suggests a simpler and potentially more interpretable way to improve physical reasoning in video models. If effective, it could reduce dependence on complex multimodal add-ons while making world models easier to inspect and control.

paper_title: Physis-Lang: Self-Evolving Language as a Physical Representation for Video World Model
paper_authors: Liming Lu, Xianzheng Ma, Wenkun He, Guanqi Zhan, Yilin Zhao
